newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Keppel Corp sinks past three-year low.
newsitem.headline: Keppel Corp sinks past three-year low.

text.p: The share price of shipping conglomerate Keppel Corporation Ltd fell to more than a three-year low of Singapore $6.25 on Monday afternoon depressed by a poor corporate outlook, analysts said.
At 0845 GMT, the shares were trading around S$6.35, down S$0.20. Volume was over 1.2 million shares.
Keppel shares had been falling despite its announcement of a bonus issue and got battered further after it adjusted for the issue on April 22.
Analysts said they have been too optimistic in their forecasts for Keppel's earnings.
"At best, the earnings look flat for this financial year ending December 31, 1997," said an analyst with a local firm.
According to the Edinburgh Financial Publication's The Estimate Directory, Keppel is expected to post a net profit of S$244.3 million against S$204.1 million last year.
He said analysts were disenchanted with the company's plans to redevelop a shipyard site in Telok Blangah, located in southern Singapore, into a prime waterfront residential and commercial area.
To-date, there have been no further details of the plans.

"Investors paid a premium for the shares compared to other stocks in the sector on prospects that Keppel would redevelop Telok Blangah. Now they have lost faith," said an analyst with a European house.
"There are also no growth prospects for its underlying core businesses," he added.
